newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: EUTHANASIA WOMEN'S FUNERAL HELD THIS MORNING
The funeral was held this morning for the South Australian woman who last week used the Northern Territory's Termially Ill Act, to end her life.
The service for Janet Mills of Naracoorte, in the State's south-east, was attended by family and close friends.
She was the second person to use the Northern Territory Act.
Mrs Mills, aged 52, decided to end her life because she was suffering from a terminal form of cancer.
RABBIT CALICI VIRUS MAY HAVE ARRIVED IN TASMANIA
The rabbit calici virus may have arrived in Tasmania.
There are reports of large numbers of rabbits dying in the Meander area in the north of the State, and preliminary tests on some carcasses suggest the presence of the virus.
The Minister for Primary Industry, Bill Bonde, says if the results are confirmed, it's highly likely the virus has been introduced by infected insects.
CARL LEWIS SET TO COMPETE AT SYDNEY MEETING
Athletics Australia has confirmed that Carl Lewis is to compete in the Sydney Athletes Grand Prix later this month.
Lewis has won nine gold medals and one silver medal over four Olympics, as well as eight gold medals at five world championships.
Now aged 35, Lewis will run in the 100 metres in Sydney but will not compete in the long jump, an event which won him a gold medal at the Atlanta Olympics.
TIM FISCHER SAYS REPUBLIC IDEA JUST A SUGGESTION
Acting Prime Minister, Tim Fischer, says his suggestion for Australia to become a republic was just a suggestion.
That follows criticism from National Party Senate leader, Ron Boswell, who yesterday said Mr Fischer had created confusion, and had been unhelpful by putting forward the suggestion.
Mr Fischer's told ABC radio, Senator Boswell's correct to say that National Party policy is to leave the consitution unchanged.
ROSCO SET FOR NEXT LAND SPEED RECORD ATTEMPT
Australian Land-speed record holder Rosco McGlashan is determined the weather won't stop his next world record attempt on Lake Gardiner in South Australia's north.
He says he's making final modifications to his jet-powered "Aussie Invader Three", which is faster than the vehicle he used to set the Australian record of 802-kilometres an hour, two years ago.
McGlashan says when he arrives at the Lake later this month, he'll be prepared for a long stay, bringing his own transportable village.
HANDGUNS STOLEN FROM CAR IN TASMANIA
Launceston police are concerned about the theft of ten modern handguns from a gun dealer's car in northern Tasmania.
The guns were in a black briefcase in the car parked in central Launceston, and the suburbs of Youngtown and Riverside, during a period at lunchtime yesterday.
They range from a small calibre Beretta to a point four-five Hyhunter and include thirty-eights, thirty-twos and a point three-oh-eight Browning.
